review.summary: I reviewed only the supplied snapshot. I found no blockers. I found one MAJOR issue: when a client-side submit succeeds, the form and its mounted live regions are replaced, so keyboard focus is lost and the success announcement may not be heard. I also found three MINOR issues. First, a stale `registrationRetry` flag stays in the URL after a successful retry; reloading the page shows the failure message and the saved answers again, which could lead to a duplicate submission. Second, a funnel runtime redirect drops the retry and submitted flags, so the user loses the error message and their saved answers. Third, the home page Suspense wrapper turns the `/` redirect into a 200 response that shows the loading skeleton and then redirects in the page, instead of an HTTP 307. There is also one NIT about the same error being announced twice. These findings come from reading code, not from running anything. They don't confirm the full latest test matrix or any screen reader testing.

findings.issue: When a JS submit succeeds, the whole form is unmounted, including the focused submit button and the always-mounted live regions. It is replaced by a newly inserted `<div role="status">` that already contains the success text.
findings.evidence: RegistrationSubmissionFeedback says it exists to "Keep live regions mounted and restore keyboard position". LeadForm never passes `successMessage` to it. On success it returns a different tree, and nothing moves focus to the success content.
findings.impact: Keyboard and screen reader users lose their place: focus drops to `<body>`. Many screen reader and browser combinations don't announce live regions that are inserted already holding content, so the outcome users most need to hear (registration done, verification needed) may never be announced. This goes against the stated goal of the repair and WCAG 4.1.3.
findings.recommended_fix: Keep one persistent live region across the error, loading and success states. For example, render the success panel inside a wrapper that exists before submit, or pass `successMessage` to RegistrationSubmissionFeedback and swap only the form body. Then move focus to the success heading or container (tabIndex=-1) after the change.
findings.required_test: Component test: submit with a mocked `ok` response. Assert that a status region existing before submit now contains the success text, and that `document.activeElement` is the success container, not the body. Manual screen reader check (NVDA or VoiceOver) that the success message is announced.

findings.area: onSubmit success branch / retry-derived initial state
findings.issue: A successful client-side resubmit doesn't remove `registrationRetry` from the URL or clear the retry context. A reload or back/forward navigation reinitialises status to `error` and fills the form with the saved draft again.
findings.evidence: Initial state is `retry?.message ? "error"`, and field defaultValues come from `retry.draft`. The success branch only calls `setStatus("success"); form.reset()` and has no `history.replaceState` or draft invalidation.
findings.impact: After a successful retry, a reload shows a failure message and the answers pre-filled, which invites a duplicate registration. This conflicts with the no-draft message, which warns users against duplicate submissions.
findings.recommended_fix: On success, call `history.replaceState` to remove `registrationRetry` and `submitted` from the URL. Also make sure the server consumes or invalidates the retry draft cookie or capability after a successful submission.
findings.required_test: Integration test: load `?registrationRetry=429` with a draft, submit successfully, then reload. Assert that no error alert appears and that the fields are not pre-filled.

findings.issue: The funnel runtime redirect builds a URL without the query string, so `registrationRetry` and `submitted` are dropped. The draft is also bound to the original `sourcePath`, so the target step can't read it.
findings.evidence: `redirect(`/lp/${encodeURIComponent(page.slug)}/${encodeURIComponent(runtime.decision.path)}`)` is called after `registrationRetryBoundary` already read the retry state for the original step path.
findings.impact: If a no-JS or fallback submit is sent back to a step that the runtime then redirects (experiment or progression rules), the user sees no failure or verification-required feedback and their saved answers are silently lost.
findings.recommended_fix: Either keep the retry and submitted query parameters through runtime redirects and resolve the draft against the original sourcePath, or have the submission API compute the return path from the rendered step instead of the logical one.
findings.required_test: Integration test: set up a funnel step that the runtime redirects. Request it with `?registrationRetry=429` and a valid draft cookie. Assert that the final rendered page shows the retry alert and the pre-filled answers.

findings.issue: Wrapping a component that only redirects in Suspense means the shell (the skeleton) streams first. The redirect then arrives as a streamed in-page redirect (meta refresh or client navigation) with a 200 status instead of an HTTP 307.
findings.evidence: HomeRedirect awaits `getCurrentVendor()` (async I/O) and then calls `redirect()`. Because it is inside a Suspense boundary, the fallback can flush before the redirect is thrown.
findings.impact: Every visit to `/` shows the skeleton briefly and pays for an extra render before redirecting. Crawlers, link previewers and non-JS clients get a 200 skeleton page instead of a real redirect. The added boundary doesn't improve the UX, since nothing on this page is ever displayed.
findings.recommended_fix: Remove the Suspense wrapper and keep HomePage as an async component that calls `redirect()` directly, so the HTTP 307 is sent before any streaming. Update the loading test assertion to match.
findings.required_test: Request `/` without and with a vendor session. Assert a 307 with `Location: /login?from=home` and `/dashboard` respectively, and that no skeleton HTML is in the body.

findings.issue: The error text is announced once as a live alert and again when the same element receives focus. On the initial retry load it is also server-rendered alert content that gets focused immediately.
findings.evidence: The same element has both `role="alert"` and `tabIndex={-1}`, and the effect focuses it when focus is lost or still on the submit button.
findings.impact: Some screen readers may read the message twice. This is a polish issue, not a functional defect.
findings.recommended_fix: Keep focus management and rely on the focus announcement, or use the live region alone. For example, drop `aria-live` from the focused node, or announce through a separate region.
findings.required_test: Manual screen reader check that the failed-submit message is announced once.
